title: Simchat Torah, lived
hook: dancing with the scroll, even if you don't know the steps
tomorrow: a month with no holidays at all. now what?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the ushpizin: ancestors welcomed by name, and their seat handed to someone in need. Guests in the booth. The week of huts ends with the scrolls coming out.
screen: `GUESTS IN THE BOOTH.` → `THE SCROLLS COME OUT.`

segments.voice: Weddings have this moment: the music changes, a circle forms, and the uncle who swears he can't dance gets pulled in anyway. Simchat Torah has the same moment, with a Torah scroll in the middle of the circle. The last lines of Deuteronomy are read, and then, right away, the first lines of Genesis. The book ends and starts over in the same breath, and so does the dancing.
screen: `THE UNCLE WHO CAN'T DANCE.` → `A SCROLL IN THE CIRCLE.` → `THE BOOK ENDS AND STARTS OVER.`

segments.voice: Simchat Torah means the joy of the Torah. The scrolls come out of the ark and are carried around the room in circles called hakafot, with singing, kids on shoulders, and plenty of people who have no idea what the steps are. Nobody's checking. When David brought the ark of God up to Jerusalem, the text says, "David danced before the LORD with all his might." With all his might, not with all his skill. So: dance anyway. And since the circle starts over today, walk back around the one we just made. Hear every note: the commandment of the shofar is listening. Ten small changes: the window between the holy days. Life comes first: when the fast puts someone at risk, eating is the commandment. The last hour: Neilah, the gates locking, one long note. A small hut is enough: open sky and a little table. Guests in the booth: the ancestors' seat goes to someone in need. Six lines, one season of holy days, and now the book begins again.
screen: `THE JOY OF THE TORAH.` · `HAKAFOT: CIRCLES WITH THE SCROLLS.` · `WITH ALL HIS MIGHT.` · `SIX LINES, ONE SEASON.` · then, large: `DANCE ANYWAY.`

segments.voice: For the sit, let your body move a little, standing or seated. Sway side to side, slowly, the way a crowd sways when it's carrying something it loves. There are no steps to get right. If a tune comes to mind, hum it under your breath and let it set the pace.
screen: `SWAY, SLOWLY.` · `NO STEPS TO GET RIGHT.` · `HUM IF A TUNE COMES.`

segments.voice: Simchat Torah: the joy of the Torah, when the last lines are read, the first begin again, and everyone circles.
Your line: dance anyway. Nobody in the circle is grading the steps, and the book has just begun again. That's the season.

howItsDone: On Simchat Torah, congregations take every Torah scroll out of the ark and dance with them in circles (hakafot), then read the end of Deuteronomy and the beginning of Genesis; children often get flags and treats.
